name: Money Forward ME
subscription_detection: Premium 'サブスクレポート' from card/bank statements; App Store and carrier billing explicitly not supported
cross_provider_coverage: Named video, music, game, book/news and shopping services (count UNKNOWN)
bill_negotiation: No negotiation found; runs fixed-cost review and switching (insurance, electricity, internet, phone) and own electricity retail
verification: None as a feature; next month's statement implicitly
business_model: Consumer premium plus fixed-cost switching and referral (MF でんき)
moat: Aggregation connections, data scale and brand (classification: distribution and data advantage; not tested here)
evidence_strength: company-reported (help pages, IR extract); not opened
how_we_lose: It already holds the detection (J1) for card/bank rails and the user relationship for 17.3M people. A cancel guide or deep link next to the existing サブスクレポート matches C02/C03 for its base at near-zero marginal cost, and it can monetise switching (C08) without us.
cheapest_credible_response_if_we_succeed: Add a per-service 'how to cancel' link and a reminder beside each detected subscription; later, partner with or acquire a concierge for hard routes.
response_cost_and_speed: Low; weeks to months (content plus UI on an existing feature). An inference, not a company statement.

name: Moneytree / Moneytree Grow (MUFG Bank subsidiary since 2025-08-29)
subscription_detection: Grow 'サブスク一覧': monthly list of automatically retrieved subscription payments (amount, date, method)
business_model: Consumer premium; MT LINK enterprise API (43 enterprise clients, dated)
moat: Regulated aggregation infrastructure plus bank ownership (distribution and infrastructure advantage)
evidence_strength: company-reported plus secondary; help page content not seen
how_we_lose: Its owner MUFG is the most natural Japanese B2B2C buyer and already owns the list and the aggregation pipe. A startup that needed MT LINK would depend on a competitor-owned pipe.
cheapest_credible_response_if_we_succeed: Put the subscription list plus 'cancel' guidance into MUFG's bank app (emot).
response_cost_and_speed: Low to medium; bank release cycles are slow (months to a year). Inference.

name: Zaim
subscription_detection: Extracts recurring payments from records; predicts due dates and plans
how_we_lose: A third free or cheap J1 tracker sets the consumer price expectation for tracking near zero.

name: Apple App Store subscriptions
subscription_detection: Complete for Apple-billed subscriptions (the user's own list)
cross_provider_coverage: All App Store-billed apps; none outside Apple billing
cancel_instructions: In-product: Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions → Cancel
cancel_on_behalf: Only the user or Apple support; developers cannot cancel
verification: UNKNOWN (expiry shown in list, not verified here)
moat: Owns the billing rail and the device
evidence_strength: secondary and community extracts; Apple pages not opened
how_we_lose: For Apple-billed subscriptions the job is already solved free and in-ecosystem, and no third party can execute. Stop condition 1 for this rail.

name: Google Play subscriptions
cancel_on_behalf: The developer can cancel via API; no third-party route found
how_we_lose: For Play-billed subscriptions the job is solved free in Play, and only the developer has a programmatic cancel. Stop condition 1 for this rail.

name: Amazon.co.jp Memberships & Subscriptions
class: Platform (merchant with its own subscription hub)
subscription_detection: Amazon-billed subscriptions incl. Prime Video channels
cancel_instructions: In-product list; channels via browser only
how_we_lose: Amazon-billed subscriptions already have a free central list and cancel surface.

name: Carrier billing portals (docomo, au, SoftBank)
subscription_detection: Continuous-charge list in each carrier portal
cancel_instructions: Portal links to the provider (docomo); au may cancel in the list (conflicting)
moat: Owns the rail and the identity
how_we_lose: Carrier-billed subscriptions are visible to the user free in the carrier portal and invisible to card-based detection, so a startup adds little on this rail without the user's carrier login.
cheapest_credible_response_if_we_succeed: Make the continuous-charge list more prominent; add in-list cancel for all.

name: Japanese card issuers and bank apps (SMBC Olive/Vpass, JCB, Rakuten Card, etc.)
subscription_detection: No subscription-list feature found in extracts (MUFG via Moneytree is CM02)
moat: Own the transaction data and the customer
how_we_lose: They hold first-party transaction data and the dispute process. If they adopt network tooling (CM09), cancellation lands where the charge is paid, without a startup.
cheapest_credible_response_if_we_succeed: License network tooling (Visa/Mastercard) or Moneytree's list.
response_cost_and_speed: Medium; months to a year. Inference.

name: Card networks: Visa Enhanced Subscription Manager (with Pinwheel); Mastercard Subscriptions Control / Smart Subscriptions
geography: North America (Visa from summer 2026; LatAm later); US (Mastercard)
cancel_on_behalf: Cancellation inside the banking app for integrated merchants (mechanism partly guided)
how_we_lose: It defines the B2B2C category globally. A Japanese issuer evaluating C07 can wait for its network's product, with an explicit motive: fewer disputes and chargebacks.

name: サブトラ
subscription_detection: Gmail payment-mail detection; AI savings suggestions (unused, duplicate, price rise)
how_we_lose: It anchors e-mail-based J1 at ¥280 a month and shows the Gmail route is workable for a small team.

name: Subcut
how_we_lose: A low-price import could cover J1 and J3 if it supports Japanese banks (UNKNOWN).

name: Manual trackers (Recur, SubFlow, サブマネ!, サブスク管理-固定費の把握, etc.)
how_we_lose: It sets the price of reminders at about zero.

name: Cancellation guide sites (解約.com; SEO how-to sites)
cancel_instructions: Yes, with source links and AI summaries
distribution: Search at the moment of intent
how_we_lose: They own the intent moment ('X 解約') in search and solve the most-reported friction (finding the page) free. This undercuts both C02 revenue and H1 acquisition.

name: Consumer centres and the 188 hotline (消費生活センター)
cancel_on_behalf: Mediation (あっせん); scope not researched here
how_we_lose: For the obstruction and dispute cases where friction is worst, a free, trusted public channel already acts, and a paid agent would compete with it.

name: Rocket Money (formerly Truebill; Rocket Companies)
user_scale: 10M+ app users (fact sheet); 2.5M members at 2021 acquisition
cancel_on_behalf: Yes: concierge team contacts merchants; 2-10 business days typical; nearly 2.5M cancellations cumulative
business_model: Premium subscription plus negotiation fees; part of a mortgage group
evidence_strength: company-reported (SEC filings, help pages, fact sheet) plus secondary
how_we_lose: Not a Japanese competitor. As a precedent it shows the model works in the US with a contractual limited power of attorney, human operations and premium plus negotiation revenue. Cancellations per user are low (about 0.25 cumulative).

name: Trim (OneMain Financial)
bill_negotiation: Now only for OneMain loan customers
how_we_lose: A precedent for the 'feature, not company' outcome: the standalone consumer service ended inside a lender.

name: Whatssub (왓섭, Korea)
cross_provider_coverage: 1,365 services identifiable (829 subscriptions plus 536 fixed costs); as-of date UNKNOWN
japan_status: Japan launch not found; overseas entry 'under review' (2021-23)
how_we_lose: A foreign entrant with an existing cancellation playbook could enter Japan if a startup proves demand.

name: Unsub.ai
how_we_lose: Shows that a guide-plus-reminder product is cheap to ship (released 2026-07-05).

name: General AI agents (ChatGPT agent mode and similar)
geography: Global (Japan availability of agent mode UNKNOWN)
cross_provider_coverage: Any web flow in the user's own session
cancel_on_behalf: Acts in the user's session, under supervision
how_we_lose: It commoditises the 'AI navigates the web cancellation flow' step (C03) at zero marginal price for users who already pay. It does not cover phone, written or in-person routes.
